sentence: A low ferritin level means the body's iron stores are low, and doctors then look for the cause, which is often blood loss.
note: LTO: low ferritin points to iron deficiency; NHS: often caused by blood loss or pregnancy

sentence: Ferritin is a protein that stores iron in the body.
note: NHS: ferritin, a protein that stores iron

sentence: The test estimates how much iron is held in store.
note: LTO: main use is estimating stored iron

sentence: Doctors order it when they suspect the body has too little or too much iron, and it is most often requested for suspected low iron.
Lab Tests Online UK calls it the most sensitive early marker of iron deficiency.
A low ferritin points to iron deficiency.
The NHS explains that when ferritin is low, there is not much iron stored in the body.
Stores can drop well below normal before the iron level in the blood itself falls, so ferritin can show the problem early.
note: LTO: ferritin stores can drop before blood iron levels fall

sentence: Low iron can exist without anaemia, and symptoms such as tiredness can still be present.
note: Devon formulary (blended summary): symptoms may also be present in non-anaemic patients with low ferritin

sentence: Ferritin can also fall when protein levels are very low, as in some cases of malnutrition.
The NHS says iron deficiency anaemia is caused by a lack of iron, often because of blood loss or pregnancy.
NHS formulary guidance lists heavy periods, bleeding in the digestive tract, coeliac disease and a poor diet among the causes.
note: Devon formulary (blended summary): menorrhagia, GI causes, coeliac, poor diet

sentence: It also lists ulcers, medicines such as aspirin and anti-inflammatory painkillers, and bowel cancer as possible digestive causes, which is why the cause is looked for.
note: Devon formulary (blended summary): ulcers, colorectal cancer, aspirin/NSAIDs/long-term PPIs; second pass to confirm

sentence: Guidance for NHS Scotland says a low ferritin should be investigated for causes such as coeliac disease.
The NHS lists tiredness, shortness of breath, noticeable heartbeats and pale skin as common symptoms.
Less common symptoms include hair loss, ringing in the ears, itchy skin, a sore tongue and a craving for non-food items.
note: NHS: hair loss, tinnitus, itchy skin, sore tongue, pica

sentence: That craving, called pica, can be for items such as ice, paper or clay.
The NHS advises seeing a GP when symptoms like these appear, and a GP appointment is the usual route for a ferritin test.
note: NHS: see a GP; GP usually takes blood test

sentence: Ferritin is not only a store of iron.
note: LTO says it can be high for non-iron reasons

sentence: Lab Tests Online UK says levels can be high in inflammatory conditions, infection and liver disease.
Because inflammation can push ferritin up and hide a shortage of iron, CRP is often checked alongside it.
note: Devon formulary: ferritin may be spuriously raised in presence of inflammation; CRP checked

sentence: A high ferritin can signal long-term iron overload, especially haemochromatosis, but further investigation is needed before that diagnosis is made.
A GP usually takes a blood test, and ferritin is the key marker of how much iron is stored.
If the cause is not clear, the GP may arrange further tests to find the source.
Once the cause has been found, such as an ulcer or heavy periods, the GP recommends treatment for it.
Iron tablets are the usual first treatment, and the NHS says they are taken for about six months.
note: NHS: iron tablets for about 6 months

sentence: Side effects of iron tablets, mainly in the digestive system, are common.
Iron can also be given by infusion into a vein, which is used less often.
Repeat blood tests over the following months check that the iron level is returning to normal.
The NHS says iron deficiency anaemia is treated with iron tablets and with iron-rich foods.
NHS guidance points to dark green leafy vegetables and dried fruit as food sources.
Formulary guidance also lists iron-fortified bread, meat, apricots, prunes and raisins.
NHS guidance says drinking orange juice after an iron tablet may help the body absorb the iron.
Tea, coffee, milk and dairy foods, and wholegrain cereals can stop the body absorbing iron from other foods and tablets.
NHS 111 Wales says iron tablets taken with or soon after food can reduce side effects, and that tablets should be continued even if side effects occur.
Somerset formulary guidance adds that treatment continues for some months after the iron level is corrected, so that stores can be replenished.
Tablets can cause constipation or diarrhoea, tummy pain, heartburn, nausea and darker stools.
A Scottish maternity guideline states that iron requirements are higher in pregnancy than in women who menstruate.
note: Greater Glasgow and Clyde guideline (blended summary)

sentence: It recommends that women who start oral iron continue it through pregnancy and for some months after the birth.
Ferritin is a protein that stores iron, so a low level means there is not much iron in store.
note: NHS: ferritin is a protein that stores iron; low means little iron stored

sentence: Ferritin can fall before blood iron levels fall, which makes it the most sensitive early marker of iron deficiency.
note: LTO: stores can drop below normal before blood iron falls; most sensitive early marker

sentence: Iron deficiency is often caused by blood loss or pregnancy, so doctors look for the source.
note: NHS: caused by lack of iron, often blood loss or pregnancy

sentence: Inflammation, infection and liver disease can raise ferritin, so it is often read alongside CRP.
note: LTO: high ferritin has other causes incl. inflammation, infection, liver disease; formulary: CRP checked alongside
